info.title: Records API
info.description: Record configurations (schemas, views, versions) and the records that conform to them. Record IDs are server-generated, config IDs are client-supplied (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`). Configs and records are updated with PUT: a config update applies only the fields sent, a record update merges `data`. Editing a config schema does not retroactively re-validate existing records. Publish a config version to snapshot the stored config; list and read versions to see its history.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: Only configs in this collection. With summary, ~default lists the configs in no collection.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Answer one page of summary rows (id, name, description, collection_id, updated_at, has_source, resolution_error) by name from the index, with total_hits. No schema or views.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: With summary: each word must prefix a word of the name or description.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. With summary, default 25, at most 1000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: With summary: rows to skip.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Without summary: the next_cursor of a truncated reply.

get.description: Returns all record configurations in the account. Each configuration defines the schema (field names, types, validation rules) and UI hints for a category of records. Call this first to discover available record types before listing or querying records. Pass `ids` to batch-fetch specific configurations instead of all.

post.description: Defines a new category of records by specifying a schema (field names, types, validation constraints) and UI rendering hints. The `id` you choose becomes the `config_id` used in all subsequent record operations for this type. Returns 409 if a configuration with the same ID already exists.

400.description: Validation error (invalid ID format, invalid schema, missing required fields)

409.description: A record configuration with the given ID already exists

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record configuration ID

get.description: Retrieves the full schema and UI layout for a specific record configuration. Use this to inspect field definitions and validation rules before creating or updating records of that type.

put.description: Updates a record configuration. Schema changes do not retroactively affect existing records.

delete.description: Deletes the configuration and its associated records storage bucket.

get.description: Search for records across a folder or space (index-backed). At least one of `folder` or `space_id` must be provided, and a Bearer JWT is required (used to derive the tenant) — an API key alone is rejected on this endpoint. `folder`/`space_id` conditions are ANDed. Results are sorted by `created_at`.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Folder ID to filter records by. At least one of `folder` or `space_id` must be provided.

parameters.name: space_id
parameters.description: Space ID to filter records by. At least one of `folder` or `space_id` must be provided.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: Comma-separated config IDs to narrow the query. One ID is ANDed with the folder/space filter; multiple IDs form an OR group.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of records to skip (pagination).

parameters.name: parent_folder
parameters.description: Records whose parent_folder equals this; ANDed with folder.

parameters.name: scope_folder
parameters.description: Records whose folder OR parent_folder equals this. Satisfies the scope requirement on its own.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: JSON `{conditions, sort_by}` over record and declared index_fields.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Field name; prefix `-` for descending. Default `created_at`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated payload paths to keep.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words ANDed; each matches any search field (text by prefix, keyword exactly). Needs one config_id.

parameters.name: search_fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated declared text or keyword index fields; defaults to every declared text field.

parameters.name: date_field
parameters.description: `created_at`, `updated_at` or a declared date index field.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD (a bare date covers its whole day).

parameters.name: latest_by
parameters.description: JSON `{"group_field":"...","order_field":"..."}`: keep the row with the highest order_field per group_field value. order_field must be a declared sortable index field. Reads one page of at most 1000 scoped rows, highest order_field first (the index page maximum; no sortable record field is unique, so deeper paging is not used); the reply carries `truncated: true` when more matched. total_hits counts groups.

400.description: Missing required filter parameter or invalid authorization token

404.description: No records found matching the query

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that records belong to

post.description: Creates a new record conforming to the specified configuration's schema. Record data is validated against the schema at creation time.

400.description: Validation error (missing required fields, type mismatch, invalid dropdown value)

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that the record belongs to

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record ID

get.description: Retrieves a single record by its ID within a given configuration. Returns the full data object and metadata (id, created_at, updated_at). Obtain the record ID from a list or query operation first.

put.description: Updates a record. Provided data fields are merged into the existing record data. The merged result is validated against the current schema.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a single record by its ID. This action is irreversible — the record's data and metadata are removed. The configuration and all other records are unaffected.

409.description: A collection with this id already exists

delete.description: Refused while any record config is still in the collection.

409.description: The collection still holds record configs

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Collection id.

post.description: Reads an already-uploaded CSV and creates one record per row, in batches. Rows go through the same validation, folder derivation, indexing and events a single create does. A row that fails is reported and the rest continue, so a partial import is visible rather than silent.

200.description: Import outcome. A 200 with a non-zero `failed` is a partial import, not a failure.

400.description: Missing config_id, neither space_id nor folder, a location outside the knowledge bucket, an unreadable file, or more rows than one import allows

404.description: Record configuration not found, or the object could not be read

delete.description: Deletes the named records of one config, each as a single-record delete would. A refused record is reported in `failed` and the rest still go; an id already gone counts as deleted. Staff only.

200.description: Delete outcome. A 200 with a non-empty `failed` is a partial delete.

400.description: Missing config_id or ids, or more than 500 ids

403.description: Client callers may not bulk delete

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration whose records are deleted

delete.description: Deletes a config's records in bulk, leaving the config itself in place. Without space_id or folder the config's whole record range is dropped in one operation. With either, only matching records are removed: the records are read a page at a time and each page's matches are deleted in concurrent batches. One call empties the scope — there is no cursor for the caller to follow — unless the reply carries `truncated`, which means records remain and the same call resumes the purge.

parameters.name: space_id
parameters.description: Purge only records in this space

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Purge only records in this folder. Matched against the record's own folder, not parent_folder.

200.description: Purge outcome. A 200 with a non-empty `failed` is a partial purge, not a failure.

400.description: Missing config_id, or the records could not be read or deleted

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration whose records are purged

get.description: Pages one record's history events, newest first. No record-existence check — a deleted record's history is still readable. `mode` in the reply is the config's CURRENT history mode, which may be `none` if history was later turned off; any retained events are still returned.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 25, clamped to 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque next_cursor from a previous page. When set, `end` is ignored — the server resumes from the cursor.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD (00:00Z that day). The server cannot bound reverse paging by a start time, so older events are dropped client-side and `next_cursor` is omitted once one is seen.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD (end of that UTC day). Applied on the first page only — ignored once `cursor` is set.

200.description: One page of history events, newest first. Snapshots are included in the list — there is no separate get-one-version endpoint.

400.description: Missing config_id or id, an unparsable start/end, or `{"code":"invalid_cursor"}` when the supplied cursor is stale or malformed.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that the record belongs to

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record ID

delete.description: Hard-erases one record's history events and time-series buckets. The record itself is untouched. Idempotent — safe to retry the same call after a partial failure.

500.description: `{"code":"history_erase_failed"}` — a partial erase; retry the same call. The body still carries `series_docs_deleted` for what completed before the failure.

post.summary: Correct a past version's stored values
post.description: Amends one put version without changing the record: `data` is materialised against the target's folded snapshot, validated against the current schema, and published as an amendment the fold applies on every future read. Refuses the record's current version (edit the record itself instead) and a hidden version. A merge that leaves the snapshot byte-identical is a no-op — 200 with the existing entry, nothing published.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that the record belongs to

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record ID

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The put event's version to act on. A deletion cannot be amended, hidden, erased or restored (400 history_target_not_put).

200.description: The folded entry as it now reads (the amended snapshot, or the unchanged existing entry when nothing changed).

400.description: Missing/invalid config_id, id or version; a malformed body; `{"code":"schema_validation_failed"}` when the merged data fails the current schema; `{"code":"history_target_not_put"}` — a delete event cannot be amended; `{"code":"history_reason_required"}` / `{"code":"history_reason_too_long"}` for `reason`.

401.description: No caller identity on the request token.

403.description: `{"code":"history_forbidden"}` — the caller's role is not in the config's `history.edit_roles` (default root and admin).

404.description: Record configuration not found, or `{"code":"history_version_not_found"}` — no event at this version.

409.description: `{"code":"history_target_is_current"}` — this is the record's current version; edit the record instead. `{"code":"history_target_hidden"}` — the version is hidden; restore it first.

500.description: `{"code":"history_read_failed"}` — could not read the version or its amendments. `{"code":"history_write_failed"}` — the amendment (or its series bucket recompute, on a timeseries config) could not be written; nothing changed.

post.description: Redacts one put version from every read — the timeline shows it as hidden, and its snapshot reads as null — without erasing the stored bytes (`.../erase` does that). Hiding the record's current version also reverts the record to the newest earlier visible version, publishing that as a new put with `restored_from` set.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that the record belongs to

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record ID

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The put event's version to act on. A deletion cannot be amended, hidden, erased or restored (400 history_target_not_put).

400.description: Missing/invalid config_id, id or version; `{"code":"history_target_not_put"}` — a delete event cannot be hidden; `{"code":"history_reason_required"}` / `{"code":"history_reason_too_long"}` for `reason`, which is required here.

401.description: No caller identity on the request token.

403.description: `{"code":"history_forbidden"}` — the caller's role is not in the config's `history.edit_roles`.

409.description: `{"code":"history_target_hidden"}` — already hidden. `{"code":"history_no_visible_version"}` — this is the current version and there is no earlier visible version to revert to; delete the record instead.

500.description: `{"code":"history_write_failed"}` — the redact could not be written (nothing changed), the series bucket recompute failed, or (when this was the current version) the record was reverted but the revert's own history event failed — the body then also carries `record`. `{"code":"history_restore_failed"}` — the version was hidden but reverting the record to the previous version failed; body carries `{"hidden": true}`.

post.description: Root and admin only, whatever `history.edit_roles` says. Secure-deletes the version's put message and every amend event holding a copy of its data; a redact stub stays in the timeline so the timeline still shows a version existed. Idempotent — safe to retry after a partial failure; erasing an already-hidden version upgrades the hide. POST rather than DELETE because a reason is required and the gateway only forwards a body reliably on POST/PUT. Erasing the record's current version also reverts it to the newest earlier visible version.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that the record belongs to

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record ID

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The put event's version to act on. A deletion cannot be amended, hidden, erased or restored (400 history_target_not_put).

400.description: Missing/invalid config_id, id or version; `{"code":"history_target_not_put"}` — a delete event cannot be erased; `{"code":"history_reason_required"}` / `{"code":"history_reason_too_long"}` for `reason`, which is required here.

401.description: No caller identity on the request token.

403.description: `{"code":"history_forbidden"}` — erase is root/admin only regardless of `history.edit_roles`.

409.description: `{"code":"history_no_visible_version"}` — this is the current version and there is no earlier visible version to revert to; delete the record instead.

500.description: `{"code":"history_write_failed"}` — the redact stub could not be written; nothing was deleted. `{"code":"history_erase_failed"}` — the stub was written but the secure delete did not complete; body carries `{"stub_written": true}` and the same call can be retried. `{"code":"history_restore_failed"}` — erased but the record could not be reverted to the previous version; body carries `{"erased": true}` (or, if the revert landed but its own history event failed to write, `{"code":"history_write_failed"}` with `record` in the body).

post.summary: Restore a past version as the record's next version
post.description: Materialises one visible put version's folded snapshot as the record's next version (or re-creates the record if it is currently deleted), validated against the current schema. A dedicated endpoint rather than a flag on the record update — the server takes the snapshot from the fold, so a caller cannot label arbitrary data as a restore, and the permission is history's, not the record's. Refuses the current version and a hidden version.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of the record configuration that the record belongs to

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record ID

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The put event's version to act on. A deletion cannot be amended, hidden, erased or restored (400 history_target_not_put).

400.description: Missing/invalid config_id, id or version; `{"code":"history_target_not_put"}` — a delete event cannot be restored; `{"code":"history_reason_too_long"}`; `{"code":"schema_validation_failed"}` — the snapshot no longer matches the current schema; `{"code":"effective_at_invalid"}`; or a plain error when the target predates full snapshots and the record is currently deleted (nothing to apply values onto).

401.description: No caller identity on the request token.

403.description: `{"code":"history_forbidden"}` — the caller's role is not in the config's `history.edit_roles`.

409.description: `{"code":"history_target_is_current"}` — this is already the current version. `{"code":"history_target_hidden"}` — restore it is not possible while hidden. `{"code":"record_exists"}` / `{"code":"record_conflict"}` — rare races on the underlying record write.

500.description: `{"code":"history_read_failed"}`. `{"code":"history_write_failed"}` — the record was saved but its history event was not; body carries the saved `record`.

get.summary: Read a time-series field across a config's records
get.description: Reads one indexed history.series.fields field from the records-series bucket index, ascending by effective_at then record_id. Backed by a daily bucket index, not the raw event stream.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: One of the config's history.series.fields.

parameters.name: record_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated record ids to narrow to, at most 50. Omitted reads every record under the config.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive lower bound on effective_at.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD (end of that UTC day), inclusive upper bound on effective_at.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Default 1000, clamped to 1000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Default 0, at most 10000.

200.description: Series points for the requested field, ascending by effective_at then record_id. Buckets whose payload lacks the field are omitted from results but counted in total_hits.

400.description: Missing config_id or field, record_ids over 50 entries, an unparsable start/end/limit/offset, `{"code":"history_not_timeseries"}` when the config's mode is not timeseries, or `{"code":"series_field_unknown"}` when field is not one of the config's series.fields.

parameters.name: config_id
parameters.description: ID of a record configuration whose history.mode is timeseries. The literal path segment "series" is matched before the {id} parameter of /records/{config_id}/{id}, so a record cannot be named "series".

get.summary: List a record configuration's published versions
get.description: Newest first, with the current published version and the numbers a minor and a major publish would take next. Any role but client and guest.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record configuration ID

get.summary: Get one published version with its snapshot

200.description: The version and its full config snapshot

400.description: version is missing or not MAJOR.MINOR

404.description: Configuration or version not found (code config_version_not_found)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record configuration ID

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Published version number, MAJOR.MINOR

post.summary: Publish the stored configuration as a new version
post.description: Snapshots the whole configuration as stored (never a draft) and makes it the current published version. The backend numbers it: MAJOR.(MINOR+1), or (MAJOR+1).0 with major. Saving a configuration never publishes it. Any role but client and guest.

200.description: The version published (or replayed for a repeated idempotency_key)

400.description: Missing or overlong title or summary

409.description: config_version_moved: another version was published since expected_current_version_id; config_changed: the configuration was saved since expected_config_revision; config_is_reference: a catalogue reference is versioned by its publisher

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Record configuration ID

post.description: Creates a record under an id the caller chose. A repeat of the same id is answered 409 with the stored record and never overwrites it or the edits made since. Takes the same body as create record, with config_id in the body.
Finds the record whose identity matches (trying identity_fields in order) or creates it, and merges data into it. Omitting parent_folder leaves an existing parent alone.

delete.summary: Delete a record while a field is unset
delete.description: Deletes the record only while data[unset_field] is unset. 200 deleted, 404 gone, 409 refused because the field is set or the record changed mid-check.

post.description: Rewrites one page of the config's records into the search index so a newly declared index field becomes filterable. Resume with the cursor from the previous reply. A record the indexer refuses is reported by id and does not stop the page.

post.summary: Email an export of a record set
post.description: Builds a CSV or JSON file of the records matching the same filter and sort strings a records query takes, and emails it as an attachment.

get.description: Returns the record count for each of the listed config ids.

get.summary: List shipped fields a config can adopt
get.description: Lists named shipped fields the account's record config does not yet have.

post.summary: Adopt shipped fields into a config
post.description: Adds the named shipped fields to the account's own record config. Nothing else in the document changes, and the config stays off the shipped track afterwards.
Evaluates metric definitions against a config's records.
Checks metric definitions without running them.
Interprets a scored record under the published policy. Takes the same roles as scoring, because the record trigger runs as whoever wrote the record.
Re-runs interpretation for one record. Staff only; writes nothing a person owns.
Re-reads the record's stored report under the connector's current definition, then re-interprets. No provider call and no meter. Staff only.
Publishes a policy, or the default policy with use_default. Admin and root only; 409 once a policy is in use.
Returns the policy profiles available to the account.
Previews a policy's effect without writing. Admin, root and developer roles.
Reports the impact of a policy across records without writing, paged by cursor. Admin, root and developer roles.
Runs the setup test for the assessment configuration.
Marks notes approved. Staff only, never a client.
Records agreement with a score. Staff only.
Approves a client report. Staff only, never a client.
Renders a client report. Without task_id it is a preview; with one it is a delivery. Staff only.
Creates a discussion note. Staff only; a refusal carries a gate code.
Records that the discussion note was signed, for a staff member. Clients are refused by role.

get.description: Reads the approval status of a record. Staff.
Reads the assessment setup checklist. Staff.
Reads assessment health, memoised server-side for about 60 seconds. Admin, root and developer roles.

post.description: Publishes a strategy version.

get.description: Reads the active strategy version unless one is named. 404 strategy_not_published when none is published.
Reads the method text of a version, or the latest. 404 for an unknown version.

post.description: Runs a stored model. 409 strategy_not_published; 422 for engine validation errors. Staff.
Runs variants against the base model's draws. Staff.
Runs one solver per call, for example sustainable spend or minimum strategy. Staff.
Re-runs the stored model and files the result beside it. Staff.

RecordPropType.description: Allowed JSON primitive/composite types for a schema field.

FormatterType.description: Display formatter applied when rendering a field value.

FieldProps.description: Display / configuration props forwarded to the input widget. `label` should always be set. Which props apply depends on the input type (e.g. `options`/`sort` for dropdown, `min`/`max`/`decimalPlace` for number/currency, `minDate`/`maxDate` for date, `includedCountries`/`showNativeName` for country, `maxItems` for multi-select).

label.description: Display label shown above/beside the input. Always set this.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text shown inside the input when empty.

helpText.description: Optional help text rendered below the input.

markdown.description: Help text content in Markdown format.

options.description: Choices for dropdown / multi-select / multi-toggle. Seed from the schema field's enum.

value.description: Machine value submitted when this option is selected.

note.description: Optional extra description shown alongside the option.

sort.description: When `true`, options are sorted alphabetically before rendering.

minDate.description: Earliest selectable date (ISO 8601). Applies to `date` / `date-range` inputs.

maxDate.description: Latest selectable date (ISO 8601). Applies to `date` / `date-range` inputs.

min.description: Minimum allowed numeric value. Applies to `number` / `currency` / `slider` inputs.

max.description: Maximum allowed numeric value. Applies to `number` / `currency` / `slider` inputs.

decimalPlace.description: Number of decimal places displayed. Applies to `number` / `currency` inputs.

maxItems.description: Maximum number of selections. Applies to `multi-select`.

includedCountries.description: Restrict the country list to these ISO codes (e.g. ["uk","ua"]). Applies to `country` / `multi-country`.

showNativeName.description: Show each country's native name. Applies to `country` / `multi-country`.

FieldUi.description: LEGACY per-schema-field renderer hint. The current model places `inputType`/`props` on the view field node instead (see ViewFieldNode); the renderer reads node config first and only falls back to this schema-level `ui` for nested object-group members and array-item leaves that are not their own view node, and the frontend strips `ui` from placed fields on save. Prefer node-level config.

FieldFormatter.description: Formatter applied when displaying a field value.

props.description: Extra props forwarded to the formatter.

FieldDisplay.description: Display configuration embedded in a schema field.

RecordSchemaField.description: Definition of a single field at any depth of the schema tree. Recurses via `properties` (objects) and `items` (arrays). Only `type` is required. Input config for a placed form field belongs on the view node (ViewFieldNode.inputType/props), NOT here; the legacy `ui` hint is a fallback only.

type.description: JSON type(s) for this field. Use an array to allow multiple types (e.g. ["string", "null"]).

properties.description: Nested field definitions for object-typed fields.

required.description: Names of required nested fields. Only meaningful when `type` is "object".

ui.description: LEGACY UI fallback (not standard JSON Schema). Prefer node-level inputType/props on the view field node; this is only read for descendants that are not their own view node and is stripped from placed fields on save.

RecordSchema.description: A JSON Schema document describing the record structure. Always a top-level object. UI and display hints (`ui`, `display`) are embedded directly in each field definition.

type.description: Must be "object" — a record schema always describes a top-level object.

properties.description: Top-level field definitions keyed by field name.

gap.description: Gap between grid cells in pixels.

RuleProperty.description: The element property a rule drives. Field nodes support all five; grid (container) nodes support `visible` only.

ElementRule.description: A conditional rule attached to a view node. `logic` is a json-logic-engine expression evaluated against the live form value ({ "var": "FieldPath" } reads another field; dotted paths allowed); at the form root it reads the whole record, inside an array-field item it reads that item. `logic` may also be a bare boolean for an unconditional state. The result sets `property` (booleans are coerced; `value` keeps the raw computed value).

logic.description: A json-logic-engine expression object, or a boolean.

description.description: One plain-English sentence describing the condition and outcome. Does not affect evaluation.

ViewGridNode.description: A grid layout container that arranges child nodes in CSS grid columns.

rules.description: Conditional rules for this container. Only the `visible` property is honoured on a grid.

ViewFieldNode.description: A leaf node that binds an input to a schema field via a dotted path. Input config lives HERE on the node — `inputType`, `props`, and `rules` — not on the schema, so one schema can back several forms with different config. Omit `inputType` to accept the type default (string→text, number/integer→number, boolean→toggle, array→tags, object→key-value).

field.description: Dotted path to the schema field (e.g. "name", "address.city"). The property key is `field` (a `ref` key is ignored by the engine).

rules.description: Conditional rules for this field. Field nodes support all five rule properties.

ViewTableColumn.description: A column descriptor in a table view.

field.description: Schema field key this column displays.

ViewTableNode.description: A table view that lists columns to display and their order.

ViewArrayFieldNode.description: A repeating container (Repeater) bound to an array-of-object schema field. `children` is a builder-authored template of view nodes for one item; each child's `field` is ELEMENT-RELATIVE — resolved against the array field's `items.properties`, not the top-level schema (e.g. for array field "products", a child field "title" means "products[].title", not "products.title"). `props` (label, required, minItems, maxItems, collapsible, defaultCollapsed) is UI-only and not enforced by records-service; array size limits still come from the schema field's own JSON Schema minItems/maxItems if set there.

field.description: Dotted path to an array-of-object schema field.

props.description: UI-only container config: label, required (at least one item), minItems, maxItems, collapsible, defaultCollapsed.

children.description: View nodes for one item, with element-relative `field` refs. Child field nodes carry their own node-level inputType/props/rules.

rules.description: Reserved — array-field rules are NOT evaluated in v1. Put rules on the child field nodes instead.

ViewNode.description: A node in the view tree — a grid container, a field leaf, an array-field repeater, or a table.

RecordForm.description: One named form for a config: metadata plus a grid layout tree. `id` is unique within the config and appears in the app URL; the migrated legacy single form always gets id "default".

RecordViews.description: UI layout definitions for different rendering contexts. `forms` (multiple named forms) is the current model. `form` (singular) is the deprecated legacy single form — the server still accepts it, but the frontend migrates it to `forms: [{ id: "default", ... }]` on read and never writes it back.

forms.description: Current model — multiple named forms per config.

form.description: Deprecated legacy single form. Use `forms` instead.

id.description: Unique identifier. Immutable after creation. Allowed characters: alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen.

description.description: Optional longer description of what this configuration represents.

label.description: Optional short label, e.g. for UI badges or tabs.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp set automatically on creation.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp updated automatically on every modification.

InputType.description: Input widget type for form rendering.

id.description: Unique identifier. Must be unique across all configurations. Allowed characters: alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen.

rules.description: A comment is required when the rating is 2 or lower.

RecordConfigUpdate.description: All fields are optional. Omitted fields are left unchanged. Schema changes do not retroactively affect existing records.

id.description: Unique identifier. Auto-generated if not provided on creation.

config_id.description: ID of the RecordConfig that defines this record's schema.

data.description: Key-value map of field values. Keys correspond to SchemaField IDs. Values must match the field type defined in the schema. Extra keys not defined in the schema are permitted.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp set automatically on creation.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp updated automatically on every modification.

RecordCreate.description: The config_id is taken from the URL path and does not need to be repeated in the body. `data` is optional (defaults to an empty object) but is validated against the config schema when present.

id.description: Server-generated record ID (10-character nanoid). Any `id` sent in the request body is ignored.

data.description: Field values validated against the configuration schema. Required schema fields must be present. Values are type-checked against the schema. Null values are accepted for optional fields. Extra keys not in the schema are allowed. If omitted, an empty object is used.

space_id.description: Optional space ID to associate the record with a specific space.

folder.description: Optional folder to organize the record into.

RecordUpdate.description: Partial update. `data` is merged key-by-key into the existing record; `folder`/`space_id` are overwritten only when supplied. The merged result is validated against the current schema.

data.description: Fields to update. Merged into the existing record data (partial update). The merged result is validated against the current schema.

space_id.description: Optional space ID to associate the record with a specific space.

folder.description: Optional folder to organize the record into.

results_total.description: Number of records returned in this response.

total_hits.description: Total matching records across all pages (returned by the query endpoint; used with limit/offset).

status_code.description: HTTP status code echoed in the response body.

SchemaFieldType.description: Data type of a schema field. Determines how record data values are validated: text/rich_text/date accept strings, number accepts floats, checkbox accepts booleans, dropdown accepts one of the predefined options.

id.description: Unique identifier for this field within the schema. Used as the key in record data.

label.description: Human-readable display name for the field.

required.description: When true, records must include a non-null value for this field.

options.description: Allowed values for dropdown fields. Required when type is 'dropdown'. Ignored for all other types.

RecordHistory.description: Per-config history declaration. Absent, or {"mode":"none"}, means history is off. Turning history on starts recording from that moment; nothing backfills.

mode.description: "audit" keeps the full record snapshot on every changed write. "timeseries" keeps only the numeric fields named in series.fields, bucketed by day.

retention.description: How long events are kept. Enforced by a retention sweeper; the underlying stream's own MaxAge is the 1095d ceiling.

series.description: Required when mode is "timeseries"; rejected on any other mode.

edit_roles.description: Roles that may amend, hide and restore this config's history. Absent or empty defaults to ["root", "admin"]. "client" is never accepted. Erase always requires root or admin regardless of this list.

fields.description: Dotted, numeric schema fields to index into daily buckets, e.g. "rate" or "metrics.high". Each must resolve through schema.properties (objects only, not array items) to a leaf typed number or integer.

RecordHistoryEntry.description: One event on a record's history.

sequence.description: Stream sequence number of this event.

time.description: When the event was written (the stream message's own timestamp, RFC3339Nano).

version.description: The record's version at this event. A delete event carries the record's version at the time of delete, plus one.

mode.description: The config's history mode at write time.

actor.description: User id from the write's own token; empty when the write carried none.

effective_at.description: The time this value is about. Defaults to write time.

config_updated_at.description: The config's updated_at at write time, for detecting schema drift against a snapshot. Empty for events written before this field existed.

snapshot.description: mode "audit": the full stored record, version included. mode "timeseries": {"<field>": <number>, ...} for series.fields only, omitting fields that were missing or non-numeric. null on a delete event, a hidden version or an erased version.

reconstructed.description: Always false in v1. Reserved for a future repair sweeper that re-derives a missed event from the record's stored version.

restored_from.description: Present only on a put that restored an earlier version: the version its snapshot was copied from.

hidden.description: True once any redact targets this version.

erased.description: True once a redact with erased:true targets this version; its stored bytes are gone and snapshot is synthesised from the redact stub.

hidden_by.description: Actor of the redact with the highest sequence targeting this version. Present when hidden.

hidden_at.description: That redact's write time. Present when hidden.

hidden_reason.description: That redact's reason. Present when hidden.

amended_by.description: Actor of the amend with the highest sequence targeting this version. Present only when edited and not hidden.

amended_at.description: That amend's write time. Present only when edited and not hidden.

amend_reason.description: That amend's reason. Present only when edited and not hidden.

original_snapshot.description: The put's own snapshot before the winning amend replaced it. Present only when edited and not hidden.

mode.description: The config's CURRENT history mode, which may differ from the mode events in this page were written under.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next (older) page. Omitted once the page reaches `start` or the history is exhausted.

amendments_truncated.description: true when this record has more than 2000 amend/redact messages and only the newest 2000 were folded onto this page; a version corrected or hidden by an older amendment could read as untouched.

RecordSeriesPoint.description: One day bucket's value for the requested field.

bucket.description: The bucket key, YYYY-MM-DD for day buckets.

version.description: The record's version when this bucket was last written. A late or corrected value overwrites the bucket and this changes.

RecordSeriesResponse.description: get.record-series reply, ascending by effective_at then record_id.

results.description: Buckets whose payload lacks the requested field are omitted here, though they still count in total_hits. Gaps are gaps — nothing interpolates.

total_hits.description: Matching buckets before the per-field filter is applied, so it can exceed results_total.

series_docs_deleted.description: Series bucket documents removed by this call. On a partial failure this is what completed before the error, and the same call can be retried.

RecordHistoryAmendRequest.description: Body of POST .../amend. `data` is merged onto the target version's folded snapshot data exactly as a record update merges (`replace: true` replaces `data` wholesale instead). `folder`, `parent_folder`, `space_id` and `completed` are not amendable.

data.description: Corrected field values, merged into the target version's data.

validate.description: Validate the merged result against the current schema. false skips validation.

hidden_fields.description: Schema fields to exclude from validation, as on a record update.

reason.description: Required, 1-500 characters after trimming. 400 history_reason_required when empty, history_reason_too_long over 500.

example.reason: Wrong close copied from the sheet

RecordHistoryReasonRequest.description: Body of POST .../hide, .../erase and .../restore. An empty or omitted body is treated as no reason. `reason` is required for hide and erase (400 history_reason_required when empty after trimming, history_reason_too_long over 500 characters); optional for restore, where it is only echoed back in the response and stored nowhere.

erased.description: Present (true) only on the erase reply.

restored.description: The record after being reverted to the previous visible version — present only when the acted-on version was the record's current one. null otherwise, and null on an erase's idempotent re-run.

version.description: The version that was restored from — the same value as restored_from, not the record's new version (that is record.version).

reason.description: Echoed from the request; omitted when none was given.

PurgeRecordsResult.description: `scanned` and `purged` are equal only on an unscoped purge, which deletes without reading. Failed records are left in place; a retry with the same scope picks them up.

scanned.description: Records read to answer the scope. On an unscoped purge, the records the config held.

failed.description: IDs of records whose delete or de-index was refused.

truncated.description: The purge stopped short of its scope: records remain, and the same call run again carries on from where it left off. Absent or false means the scope is empty.

CsvImportRequest.description: Turn an already-uploaded CSV into records. The file is named, not carried: upload it to the knowledge object bucket first and send its location, so a file of any size travels once rather than through this request body.

config_id.description: Configuration the records are created under.

object_uri.description: Location of the uploaded file, as obj://<bucket>/<key>. Only the microstrate-agent-knowledge bucket may be read.

bucket.description: The same location spelled out, for a caller that has it apart. object_uri wins if both are given.

column_map.description: CSV heading to record field name. A heading absent from the map is ignored, which is how a column is dropped. An empty map falls back to the sanitised heading.

types.description: Record field name to column type, so values are coerced exactly as the caller's preview showed them. A field missing here is written as text.

space_id.description: Space every created record is filed under.

folder.description: Folder every created record is filed under. Omitted, each record's folder is derived from its identity, exactly as a single create does.

parent_folder.description: Parent folder every created record hangs off.

batch_size.description: Records written concurrently. Clamped to the service maximum.

completed.description: Mark each record complete, which fires its record trigger. Off by default: an import is a bulk load, and firing a workflow per row is a deliberate choice.

validate.description: Hold each imported row to the configuration schema, as a typed record is. False lets partial rows through.

CsvImportResult.description: created + failed always equals total. `errors` is capped; `failed` is exact.

total.description: Data rows read from the file, excluding the header.

errors.description: The first failures only, so a wholly invalid file does not reply with one entry per row.

row.description: 1-based, counting data rows only — the spreadsheet line number minus one.

history_failed.description: Rows created (and counted in `created`) whose history event was not written. Omitted when 0.

restored_from_version_id.description: Set only when the snapshot equals that version's exactly

next_version.description: The number a minor publish would take, MAJOR.MINOR

next_major_version.description: The number a major publish would take, MAJOR.0

expected_current_version_id.description: The current version the caller saw; empty for none

expected_config_revision.description: The configuration revision the caller saw (revision on a configuration read)

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry after a lost reply safe, but only when the retry also sends expected_current_version_id

oauth2.description: API integration client credentials. Tokens only work on the task-sync routes in workspaces.

tags.name: Record Configs
tags.description: Manage record configuration schemas. Each configuration defines the structure (fields, types, validation rules) that records must conform to.

tags.name: Records
tags.description: Manage individual data records. Each record belongs to exactly one configuration and its data is validated against that configuration's schema.

tags.name: Record Config Versions
tags.description: Published snapshots of a record config.

tags.name: Record History
tags.description: The change history of a record.
